# STM32H743 Nano FC + 4-in-1 ESC (Job #52): Architecture, Loss Model, DShot Allocation, Netlist

## 0. Architecture and Feasibility

Before the derivation, two points that affect everything below.

**1. The 48 kHz PWM is not generated by the H743.** The H743 is the flight controller. It sends DShot600 to four ESC microcontrollers, one per motor. This document assumes AT32F421-class MCUs running AM32, which supports 48 kHz PWM and bi-directional DShot. Each ESC MCU drives a three-phase gate driver and six MOSFETs. The switching-loss model applies to that ESC stage.

**2. An "80 A burst" on a nano (20×20 mm) board is thermally marginal.** The model in §2 shows it is survivable only for about 1 s with all four channels loaded. Treat 80 A as a single-channel transient rating. Use roughly 35–45 A as the continuous rating at most. Section 2.5 quantifies this. If the requirement is genuinely 4×80 A sustained for several seconds, the board must grow to 30.5×30.5 mm with 5×6 mm FETs.

## 1. Conduction Loss Model (80 A burst)

### 1.1 Current path
AM32 uses six-step commutation with complementary (synchronous) PWM. At every instant, the phase current flows through two devices:
- During the on-time D: one high-side FET (HS) and one low-side FET (LS).
- During the off-time (1−D): the LS of the active leg and the LS of the return leg.

So the current always sees two channel resistances, independent of D:

$$P_{cond,ch} = I^2 \cdot 2 R_{DS}(T_j) + I^2 R_{cu}$$

### 1.2 Temperature-dependent R_DS(on)

$$R_{DS}(T_j) = R_{25}\left[1 + k(T_j - 25)\right],\quad k \approx 0.005\ /\mathrm{K}$$

At T_j = 125 °C, R_DS = 1.5 mΩ.

### 1.3 Numbers at 80 A

$$P_{FET} = 80^2 \times 2 \times 1.5\,\mathrm{m\Omega} = 19.2\ \mathrm{W}$$

$$P_{cu} = 80^2 \times 0.5\,\mathrm{m\Omega} = 3.2\ \mathrm{W}$$

That is about 9.6 W per conducting FET. This is a positive-feedback system: R_DS(on) rises with T_j. Solve iteratively with §2.4. At 25 °C the FET loss would be 12.8 W.

## 2. Switching Loss Model at 48 kHz

### 2.1 Transition time from gate charge

$$I_{g,on} = \frac{V_{drv} - V_{pl}}{R_{g,tot}} = \frac{10 - 3.5}{2.5} = 2.6\ \mathrm{A}$$

The driver limits this to about 1.5 A, so

$$t_{gd} = \frac{Q_{gd}}{I_g} \approx 6.7\ \mathrm{ns}$$

Add common-source inductance, di/dt limiting, and the Q_gs2 interval. Use t_r ≈ t_f ≈ 15 ns as the design value. Measure this on the prototype with a ≥500 MHz probe on the switch node.

### 2.2 Loss components (hard-switched HS)

| Term | Formula | Value |
|---|---|---|
| V·I overlap | ½·V·I·(t_r + t_f)·f_sw = ½·25.2·80·30 ns·48 kHz | 1.
